source.title: The Missing Curve Detectors of InceptionV1: Applying Sparse Autoencoders to InceptionV1 Early Vision

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. There is a minor source-text corruption in an appendix reference, which appears as “??”.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse autoencoders to InceptionV1, a convolutional neural network rather than an LLM or toy network, and reports feature-level results in this new setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE feature interpretations and branch-localization findings. Its model is InceptionV1, not an LLM, so these results do not test V4 as worded. The cited toy-model and earlier InceptionV1 results are not recorded as findings of this study.
record.test_reason: Applies SAEs to InceptionV1, a vision CNN. It reports that a real non-LLM model contains sparse interpretable features an SAE recovers and that features spread across neurons and branches (V4, new setting). It also shows the SAE decomposition shifts with the L1 coefficient and misses cross-branch features (bears on V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAEs reveal interpretable InceptionV1 features invisible at the neuron level, including missing curve detectors, and split some polysemantic neurons. They say SAEs' promise extends beyond language models, and frame the paper as an early, non-systematic report.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains SAEs on InceptionV1 image activations and examines feature examples, visualizations, synthetic curve responses, and branch localization; it does not reproduce the toy-model method or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Higher L1 coefficients change the relative maximum activations of the double-curve and single-curve features. Branch-specific versus all-branch SAE training is also considered; the authors note that cross-branch superposition is more significant than initially expected.

fits_no_version.finding: Features concentrated on the 5x5 branch are disproportionately curve detectors, matching prior branch-specialization work.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In InceptionV1, SAE features show branch specialization, with curve detectors most localized to the 5x5 branch.

record.problems: The authors explicitly describe the report as very early and say they do not aim to defend the generality of the examples systematically. Several appendix findings are preliminary; numerical uncertainty estimates and controls are not reported. The branch-specific main SAEs omit cross-branch interactions, which the appendix says may be significant.
record.rows_left_out: No reported claim-relevant results were left out.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of capacity or importance as the cause of polysemanticity.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemantic neurons.
LLMs are not studied; evidence is only from the InceptionV1 CNN.
Canonicality and completeness are not measured systematically. There are no cross-seed or cross-size comparisons and no reconstruction metrics.
Does not test whether features are one-dimensional.

missing.what: The authors' statement that branch-specific SAEs will have features still hidden by cross-branch superposition. This incompleteness of the main SAEs is not its own row.
missing.locator: Appendix A, final paragraph; Section 2.1.2 parenthetical

missing.what: Figure 1 interpretable feature examples for conv2d0, conv2d2 and mixed3a, each paired with a polysemantic or vaguely related nearest neuron. Only conv2d1 and mixed3b are rowed.

record.verdict_notes: V4 is worded for LLMs but its text says 'real models'. The link here treats a vision CNN as a new setting (T3); a stricter reading would set V4 to none and route the findings to fits_no_version. All evidence is qualitative: no counts, uncertainty or controls are given. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether limited capacity or feature importance causes neurons to be dedicated or shared.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Reports SAE results on InceptionV1, not LLMs; does not test the stated LLM claim.
Does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Uses feature directions in its SAE decomposition but does not test whether the model's represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Analyze SAE feature activations and their corresponding neurons
rows.measure: Qualitative feature interpretability and neuron correspondence
rows.value: The SAE feature is described as a relatively monosemantic brightness-gradient detector; its most involved neuron was not categorized by earlier work and appears polysemantic.
rows.note: The paper says the SAE decomposes conv2d1/n/44 into features responding to brightness gradients of various orientations, colour contrast, and complex Gabor filters.
rows.check: Linked to none. It shows the SAE recovering a monosemantic feature from a polysemantic neuron in a real model. Setting is a CNN, not an LLM.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Analyze SAE feature activations and their corresponding neurons
rows.measure: Qualitative feature interpretability and neuron correspondence
rows.value: The SAE feature is described as a relatively generic boundary detector; the corresponding neuron responds to boundaries with a preference for fur on one side. The SAE appears to separate generic and fur-specific boundary features in the same orientation.
rows.note: Qualitative example; no numerical feature or neuron scores are reported.
rows.check: Linked to none. SAE splits a neuron into generic and fur-specific boundary features. CNN setting.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Test SAE curve-detector features with synthetic curve stimuli across orientations and radii

conditions.value: Synthetic curves across a range of orientations and radii

rows.baseline: Known curve-detector neurons and gaps in their orientation coverage
rows.value: The authors report SAE curve-detector features matching known curve-detector neurons and additional features filling several gaps where no neuron responds to curves in a given orientation.
rows.note: The figure presents a subset of the new curve detectors; the text gives no count for the additional features.
rows.check: Linked to none. SAE recovers curve-detector features not visible among neurons. No count of new features is given.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Analyze SAE decomposition of a neuron identified as a double curve detector
rows.baseline: The neuron is described as a double curve detector
rows.value: It primarily decomposes into three features: two monosemantic curve detectors and one double curve detector.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative decomposition, not numerical feature weights.
rows.check: Linked to none. A double-curve neuron decomposes into constituent curve features.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Compare analogous SAE features from two additional SAEs trained with higher L1 coefficients

conditions.value: Higher than the original SAE; exact values not stated

rows.measure: Maximum activations of analogous double-curve and single-curve features
rows.baseline: Original SAE; exact baseline values not stated
rows.value: As L1 increases, the analogous double-curve feature's maximum activation falls, while the left- and right-curve features' maximum activations increase.
rows.note: The paper describes the direction of change; the figure's values are not transcribed in the text.
rows.check: Linked to none. The decomposition changes with the L1 coefficient: the double-curve feature shrinks as the single-curve features grow. So the SAE features are not stable across a hyperparameter choice. The authors suspected the double-curve feature was an SAE failure. Exact values are only in a figure.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Measure how jointly trained SAE features are represented across mixed3b branches
rows.measure: Share of positive-weighted neurons on the 5x5 branch
rows.value: Some features are as much as 80% localized to 5x5; others are nearly 0% localized there. The authors say many features appear to be spread across branches.
rows.note: Negative weights were excluded when computing the norm. The paper says no feature is represented entirely on the 5x5 branch.
rows.check: Linked to none. Many features spread across branches, so features are distributed over neurons (V4). The authors say branch-specific SAEs leave features 'still hidden by cross-branch superposition', i.e. incomplete dictionaries (V5). Baseline is not applicable.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Preliminary analysis of feature localization across mixed5b branches
rows.value: A small fraction of features are very concentrated on the 5x5 branch, while most are more distributed.
rows.note: No numerical fraction or feature count is stated.
rows.check: Linked to none. Most mixed5b features are distributed across branches. Preliminary, with no numbers.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Preliminary analysis of feature localization across mixed4e branches
rows.value: mixed4e preliminarily looks more similar to mixed3b in branch specialization.
rows.note: The paper does not specify the measured distribution or a numerical result for mixed4e.
rows.check: Preliminary qualitative statement only, with no distribution reported in the text.

relationships.condition: InceptionV1 CNN early-vision layers (non-LLM setting), SAE features judged qualitatively
relationships.reason: The SAE recovers interpretable features hidden in polysemantic neurons (R1-R4), and features are spread across branches (R6, R7). Evidence is qualitative and from a CNN, not an LLM.
relationships.display_finding: The SAE recovered interpretable features hidden in polysemantic neurons, and features were spread across branches. The evidence is qualitative and comes from a CNN, not a language model.

relationships.condition: InceptionV1 mixed3b SAEs varying the L1 coefficient and the branch-specific vs. joint training scope
relationships.reason: The double- vs. single-curve decomposition shifts with L1 (R5). Branch-specific SAEs miss features hidden across branches (R6). So the features depend on SAE choices and are incomplete.
relationships.display_finding: The split into double- and single-curve features shifted with the L1 coefficient, and branch-specific SAEs missed features spread across branches.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
